_note: Out-of-audio canon spliced into the clean transcript. The ancestral-vision sequence was delivered to the table as storyboard pages, not spoken, so none of it exists in the diarized audio — every entry here is marked as a storyboard insert and none of it claims a microphone. Speaker resolution is a semantic decision recorded below, exactly like the shared-mic decisions: nothing is inferred at render time.
delivery: GM sent the pages to the players mid-session (L1645-L1660: 'hopefully you just got a text from me' / 'Now you read the whole thing. You're experiencing all these visions'). The players read them silently, which is why the audio jumps straight from the setup to the reactions at L1677-L1709.

anchor.why: L1660 is the GM telling the table to read the whole vision; L1677 onward is the table reacting to it. The vision belongs between the two.

speakers._note: Storyboard bubble label -> identity. `NPC:<Name>` is a GM-voiced NPC; a bare name must be a character the session config declares. Keys of the form `p<page>.<panel>:<label>` disambiguate a label that means different people on different panels. Every label the extractor finds must appear here or the render fails.

speaker_notes.p3.1:left / p3.1:right: The storyboard labels these bubbles only by position. `The Clans - Origin.md` names them: 'The tree remembers the fire! I am Mwangi' and 'Fire remembers the tree! I am Brakkan'.
speaker_notes.moss leader / Mizizi leader: Both panels' plain-language fallbacks name Mwangi explicitly.
speaker_notes.Trench leader: Named in the source document: 'I am Barnaby, Lord of the Trench'. The 'copper-clad diver' of Act III is the same character.
speaker_notes.Fulgur leader: 'I am Astra of the Cloud Peak'.
speaker_notes.Iggy / Ignatius / Lomi: Page 1 frames the present-day scene, so these bubbles put words in the PCs' mouths. They are the GM's storyboard dialogue, not something the players said on mic, and the render labels them that way.
